name: Document accessibility review
summary: Before a designed report, deck or publication goes out, the designer gets a findings list on its headings, reading order, image descriptions, tables and contrast, with every check that could not be made named. The designer verifies each finding; the publication owner approves the fixes.

sources.title: FullyPowered AI's own published map of design work, and its own method for turning a designer's lists of how one finished document is built into a findings list in five areas.

sources.contribution: The ideas behind several checks, in our own words: a description that is filled in but tells the reader nothing, such as a file name or a single general word; an informative image wrongly marked as decorative; contrast over gradients and pictures listed as unmeasured, not counted as meeting the threshold; the usual thresholds of 4.5 to 1 for other text and 3 to 1 for large text; every slide needs a title, heading levels must not jump, a table needs a header row and merged cells are noted; the residue a check cannot see (colour used alone, captions and transcripts, link wording, document language); and an unchecked or clean result is never a pass and no conformance is claimed.
